description: The always-on keeper's region quota pre-filter: narrows the zone list to regions that actually have GPU quota before trying to create a box, so a zone-by-zone create loop does not spam 'no quota in this region' for regions that were never going to work. Extracted from the DNA-Entropy-Genbank prototype (commit 8026bf5c4afbe3021c1f7e79a17a93af4eaad84b) before its cloud/ package was gutted (issue #280/#284). Reproduces dna_entropy.cloud.keeper._apply_quota_health(cfg, all_zones, project) -> None (mutates cfg.zones in place), matching tests/test_keeper.py's 3 cases (test_apply_quota_health_narrows_to_quota_regions / _keeps_all_when_query_unknown / _keeps_all_when_zero_quota_everywhere).
function_signature: _apply_quota_health(cfg: CloudConfig, all_zones: list[str], project: str) -> None

source.repo: DNA-Entropy-Genbank (local checkout, matches the migration inventory commit exactly)
source.generated_by: worker/scratch_gen_keeper_fixtures.py, run once against that checkout's own .venv (Python 3.12.10), then deleted (not committed -- see issue #213's closing report for the exact command)
source.verified: Every case here was produced by actually CALLING the prototype's real _apply_quota_health() with a CloudConfig() and a monkeypatched gcloud.list_region_gpu_quota, then reading the real cfg.zones it mutated.

float_and_timestamp_warning: The prototype's raw captured stdout contains a `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS]` wall-clock timestamp per line -- not part of this fixture, same reason as keeper_setup_diagnosis.json. `result_zones` (a list of zone name strings, no floats) is exact and safe to compare directly.

cases.note: None means the quota query itself failed (transport error, permission, etc.) -- distinct from an empty dict below. Cannot tell whether quota exists, so keeps every zone rather than narrowing on missing information.

expected_substrings: No GPU quota found in ANY region for this project (this is the fixable part).
Your project has no L4 GPU quota yet
cases.note: An empty dict (query succeeded, genuinely zero quota everywhere) still keeps every zone -- the prototype's own comment explains why: 'the quota API under-reports' sometimes, so the real per-zone create error is still a more trustworthy final answer than trusting this query's zero outright. Same None-vs-{} distinction as cloud_quota_parsing.json and keeper_setup_diagnosis.json's flags_no_quota case.

port_note: This narrowing logic (only try zones in regions with confirmed quota) is directly useful for the C# zone/offer escalation ladder (design section 5.4, appendix B section 4.4) regardless of the always-on-keeper context it originally ran in -- unlike keeper_next_action.json's decision table, THIS behavior is not tied to the singleton-box concept D1 removes; it is a per-attempt optimization that applies equally to a per-job VM create.
